Title: Set up Django + DRF project skeleton with layered app structure
User Story: As a developer, I want a Django/DRF project split into the layers from the design spec so that every team member can build their component independently.
Acceptance Criteria: Django 4.x project `mlme` created with apps: accounts (C3), datasets (C4/C5/C12), mlengine (C6/C7/C8), reports (C9), audit (C10) | requirements.txt pins Django, djangorestframework, pandas, scikit-learn, numpy, reportlab, pytest, pytest-django, coverage, flake8 | SQLite configured for dev; settings read SECRET_KEY/DEBUG from environment | `python manage.py runserver` starts and `/api/health` returns 200 | README has local setup steps

Title: Enable GitHub Actions CI for pushes and pull requests
User Story: As a team, we want every PR automatically linted and tested so that broken code never reaches main.
Acceptance Criteria: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs flake8 and pytest with coverage on every PR and push to main | `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` fails a PR that does not reference an issue (Closes #N) | Branch protection on main: PR required, 1 approving review, CI must pass | Coverage report uploaded as a workflow artifact

Title: User registration with unique email and secure password storage
User Story: As a guest, I want to register with my email and a password so that I can use the evaluator.
Acceptance Criteria: POST /api/auth/register creates a user for a unique email and password of 8+ characters | Duplicate email returns 409/400 with a clear message; password under 8 characters rejected | Password stored only as a salted PBKDF2 hash (Django default); never logged | Register page in the UI with inline error messages

Title: Login and logout
User Story: As a registered user, I want to log in and log out so that my work is tied to my account and my session ends when I leave.
Acceptance Criteria: POST /api/auth/login starts a session for valid credentials; invalid credentials show an error | POST /api/auth/logout ends the session immediately | After logout, protected pages redirect to login (browser Back does not show data) | Login page and a dashboard landing page exist

Title: Owner-only access control on datasets and evaluations
User Story: As a user, I want only me to see my datasets and results so that my data stays confidential.
Acceptance Criteria: All dataset/evaluation querysets are filtered by request.user | Requesting another user's dataset or evaluation ID returns 404/403 | Admin-only routes return 403 for regular users | Unit tests cover the IDOR cases

Title: CSRF, XSS and SQL-injection baseline protections
User Story: As the system owner, I want framework protections switched on so that common web attacks fail.
Acceptance Criteria: CSRF middleware active; state-changing POST without token returns 403 | All templates use auto-escaping; no `|safe` on user content | Only ORM queries used (no raw SQL with string formatting) | Test proves `<script>` in a dataset name is rendered escaped

Title: Upload a CSV dataset (up to 50 MB)
User Story: As a user, I want to upload a CSV file so that I can evaluate models on my own data.
Acceptance Criteria: POST /api/datasets accepts multipart field `file` from an authenticated user | File saved to file storage (C12) under a generated name, metadata row saved in DB | GET /api/datasets lists only the user's own datasets | Upload page in the UI shows progress and success/error message

Title: Validate uploaded files and reject invalid ones
User Story: As a user, I want invalid files rejected with a specific reason so that I know what to fix.
Acceptance Criteria: Checks: .csv extension, text/csv MIME, size <= 50 MB, header row, >= 2 columns, >= 20 rows | Each failure returns a specific error code/message (400/413/415) and nothing is stored | File is parsed with pandas only; never executed or unpickled | Formula-like cells (e.g. `=cmd()`) treated as plain text | Unit tests for each rejection case

Title: Preview first 20 rows with detected column types
User Story: As a user, I want to preview my dataset so that I can check it uploaded correctly before training.
Acceptance Criteria: GET /api/datasets/{id}/preview returns first 20 rows and a dtype per column | Preview table rendered in the UI within 3 seconds for a 5 KB file | Owner-only access enforced

Title: Select target and feature columns
User Story: As a user, I want to choose the target column and feature columns so that the model learns what I care about.
Acceptance Criteria: Configure page lists columns; exactly one target and one or more features required | Target cannot also be a feature | Task type (classification/regression) inferred from target dtype and shown to the user | Saved through PUT /api/datasets/{id}/config

Title: Handle missing values (drop / mean-mode impute / none)
User Story: As a user, I want to pick how missing values are handled so that training does not fail on incomplete data.
Acceptance Criteria: Options: drop rows, mean (numeric) / mode (categorical) imputation, none | Chosen strategy stored in dataset config and applied in the data pipeline before training | Categorical features one-hot encoded in the pipeline | Unit tests for each strategy

Title: Configure train/test split size and random seed
User Story: As a user, I want to set the test size and seed so that my results are reproducible.
Acceptance Criteria: Test size accepted between 10% and 50%, default 20%; out-of-range values rejected with a range message | Random seed field (default 42); same seed gives the same split | Stratified split used for classification targets

Title: Model catalogue for classification and regression
User Story: As a user, I want to choose from a list of standard models so that I can compare algorithms.
Acceptance Criteria: GET /api/models returns: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, KNN, SVM (classification); Linear Regression, Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest Regressor (regression) | Each entry lists its editable hyperparameters with defaults | UI shows only models matching the dataset's task type; multiple can be selected

Title: Train selected models asynchronously with status tracking
User Story: As a user, I want training to run in the background with a visible status so that the page stays responsive and failures are clear.
Acceptance Criteria: POST /api/evaluations creates one job per selected model with status queued | Job manager (thread pool) moves status queued -> running -> completed/failed | UI polls GET /api/evaluations/{id} and shows the status | A failing job stores a readable error_message and does not crash the server; the next job still runs | Hard timeout of 120 s per job

Title: Classification metrics and confusion matrix
User Story: As a user, I want accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and a confusion matrix so that I can judge a classifier.
Acceptance Criteria: Metrics computed on the test split and stored with the evaluation | Weighted averaging for multi-class precision/recall/F1 | Results page shows the four metrics (0 to 1) and a confusion-matrix heatmap/table | Unit tests compare against scikit-learn on a fixed dataset

Title: Regression metrics (MAE, MSE, R²)
User Story: As a user, I want MAE, MSE and R² so that I can judge a regression model.
Acceptance Criteria: Metrics computed on the test split and stored with the evaluation | Results page shows MAE, MSE, R² and hides classification-only metrics | Unit test with a known regression dataset

Title: Sprint 1 demo video, deviation notes and sprint review
User Story: As a team, we want a recorded demo of the working Sprint 1 product so that progress is evidenced in the repo.
Acceptance Criteria: 1-minute screen recording: register -> login -> upload -> configure -> train -> view metrics | Video uploaded to `demo/sprint1_demo.mp4` (or linked in README if too large) | Any changes from SRS/SAD/Test Plan recorded in docs/6_Deviations_Log.md | Unfinished Sprint 1 items moved to Sprint 2 on the board

Title: Edit model hyperparameters
User Story: As a user, I want to change at least two hyperparameters per model so that I can tune performance.
Acceptance Criteria: Hyperparameter form per selected model, pre-filled with defaults | Values validated against allowed type/range before the job starts; invalid values rejected with a message | Hyperparameters used are stored with the evaluation and shown on the results page

Title: Side-by-side comparison table and bar chart
User Story: As a user, I want to compare two or more evaluated models so that I can pick the best one.
Acceptance Criteria: GET /api/evaluations/compare?ids=... returns metrics for the user's own evaluations | Compare page shows a table and a Chart.js bar chart with matching values | Selecting fewer than 2 evaluations shows a prompt; mixing classification and regression is blocked

Title: Export evaluation report as PDF and CSV
User Story: As a user, I want to download a report so that I can share or submit my results.
Acceptance Criteria: GET /api/evaluations/{id}/report?format=pdf|csv returns a downloadable file | Report contains dataset name, model, hyperparameters, split settings and all metrics | PDF built with ReportLab; if PDF fails, CSV still works (500 INTERNAL_ERROR for PDF only)

Title: Evaluation history: view and delete
User Story: As a user, I want to see and delete my past evaluations so that I can manage my work.
Acceptance Criteria: History page lists the user's evaluations (date, dataset, model, key metric, status) | Opening an entry shows its full results | DELETE /api/evaluations/{id} and DELETE /api/datasets/{id} remove records and stored files | Deleted items cannot be retrieved afterwards

Title: Admin: view, deactivate and delete users
User Story: As an administrator, I want to manage user accounts so that I can remove misuse.
Acceptance Criteria: GET /api/admin/users, PATCH /api/admin/users/{id} (activate/deactivate), DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} | Deactivated users cannot log in | Deleting a user removes their datasets and evaluations | Admin UI page; regular users get 403

Title: Audit logging and admin audit-log viewer
User Story: As an administrator, I want an audit log of logins, uploads, runs and admin actions so that actions are traceable.
Acceptance Criteria: AuditLog model records timestamp, user ID, action, target and IP for: login success/failure, upload, evaluation run, admin action | GET /api/admin/audit-log with filters by user and date range | Audit-log page for admins; no passwords or dataset contents logged

Title: Session timeout and account lockout
User Story: As the system owner, I want idle sessions to expire and brute-force logins to be locked out so that accounts are protected.
Acceptance Criteria: Session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity | 5 consecutive failed logins lock the account for 15 minutes; correct password rejected during lock | Lockout events written to the audit log

Title: API rate limiting (100 requests/min per user)
User Story: As the system owner, I want per-user rate limits so that the server is not overloaded.
Acceptance Criteria: DRF throttling: 100 requests/minute per authenticated user | Excess requests return HTTP 429 in the standard error format | Test sends 150 requests and asserts 429 after the 100th

Title: Docker deployment with HTTPS (Nginx + Gunicorn)
User Story: As an evaluator, I want to run the app on a fresh machine quickly and securely so that the demo is reliable.
Acceptance Criteria: Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml (app, Nginx); `docker compose up` starts the app | Nginx redirects HTTP to HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ (self-signed cert for demo) | SECURE_* Django settings enabled in production mode | Fresh-machine setup timed at 15 minutes or less and documented in README

Title: Reach 70% unit-test coverage on ML and data modules
User Story: As a team, we want solid unit-test coverage so that the core logic is trustworthy and maintainable.
Acceptance Criteria: pytest tests for data pipeline, model selector, ML engine and dataset validation | `coverage report` shows >= 70% for datasets and mlengine apps | CI fails if coverage drops below 70% on these modules

Title: Performance and load testing
User Story: As a team, we want measured performance so that we can show the NFR targets are met.
Acceptance Criteria: Locust (or similar) script: 20 concurrent users for 5 minutes, error rate <= 1% | 95th-percentile page load <= 3 s recorded | Each catalogue model trains on a 10,000 x 20 dataset in <= 60 s | Results written to docs/test_results/performance.md

Title: Usability and cross-browser testing
User Story: As a team, we want to confirm first-time users and all supported browsers work so that the demo goes smoothly.
Acceptance Criteria: 3 first-time users complete upload -> evaluate in <= 5 minutes (timings recorded) | TC-03, TC-04, TC-07 pass on latest Chrome, Firefox and Edge | Results written to docs/test_results/usability_browser.md

Title: Final documentation, Sprint 2 demo video and code freeze
User Story: As a team, we want complete documentation and a recorded final demo so that the project can be evaluated.
Acceptance Criteria: 2-minute Sprint 2 demo video uploaded to `demo/sprint2_demo.mp4` (or linked) | README: features, setup (local + Docker), screenshots, team, test results | Traceability matrix updated with test results; deviations log complete | Release tag v1.0 created; development frozen
